input.name: paperless-invoice 0.0.2 rejects ordinary 19% VAT line items

input.title: @powerhousedao/paperless-invoice 0.0.2 rejects ordinary 19% VAT line items whose gross is a round number
input.content:
**Observed 21 Aug 2026** while importing AI-extracted invoice data into a `powerhouse/invoice` document from `@powerhousedao/paperless-invoice@0.0.2`.

`ADD_LINE_ITEM` is rejected with `Tax inclusive/exclusive unit prices failed comparison` for an ordinary German VAT line: net unit price 84.03, tax rate 19%, gross unit price 100.00. The arithmetic is the whole story — 84.03 x 1.19 = 99.9957, which is not exactly 100.00. The check therefore appears to compare the two prices with exact floating-point equality and no rounding tolerance.

Why this is not an edge case: round gross prices are the normal shape of a consumer- or small-business invoice in Germany. Any line quoted as "100.00 including VAT" produces a net figure that cannot reproduce the gross exactly at 19%, because 100/1.19 is not representable to two decimal places. The rejection is therefore triggered by the most ordinary data the model will ever see, not by unusual data.

**Consequence.** Plausible German invoices cannot be imported into the invoice model at all, and extraction quality is irrelevant to the outcome — the values in this case were correct. Every other field on the same invoice imported without complaint, which locates the problem precisely: one comparison inside `ADD_LINE_ITEM`, not the extraction, not the mapping, and not the surrounding document.

**Whose finding this is.** This is a report for liberuum, the author of `@powerhousedao/paperless-invoice`, not a defect in the paperless sync package. The sync package supplied correct values and the model refused them. Recording it here rather than fixing it locally is deliberate: the validation belongs in the invoice model's reducer, so a workaround in the sync package (nudging net prices until the product lands on the gross) would be the sync inventing data to satisfy someone else's assertion.

**What resolution would look like.** A tolerance on the comparison sized to the currency's minor unit — accept the pair when the recomputed value rounds to the stated one — rather than exact equality. That is a decision for the package author, which is why this is filed OPEN rather than resolved.

**Status of the claim conflict.** The vault holds that the invoice model generates formal payment requests and that the Paperless demo's proof is a structured record produced from a scanned document. Both are premised on ordinary invoices being representable. Until the comparison is loosened, that premise is false for a common class of German invoices, and the demo's headline claim cannot be shown on such an invoice.
input.description: ADD_LINE_ITEM fails with 'Tax inclusive/exclusive unit prices failed comparison' because net 84.03 x 1.19 = 99.9957 is compared against gross 100.00 with no rounding tolerance, so plausible German invoices cannot be imported.

input.resolution: Resolved: the claim as written — that plausible German invoices cannot be imported at all — is false, and the note now carries the verified workaround. Supplying unitPriceTaxExcl at six or more decimals (84.033613 rather than 84.03) passes validatePrices; four decimals does not. The underlying defect is confirmed unfixed at 0.0.3, where validatePrices is byte-identical to 0.0.2, and stays tracked as a note plus a health recommendation for the package owner: EPSILON = 1e-5 should be a half-cent tolerance, or both prices should be compared after rounding to currency precision.
